argument: Found in Structural risk indicators, page 5 (including footnote 4). PAT005 doctrine: 'identifies entities connected through a shared address,' with indicators 'Twenty entities registered at same address' and 'Address linked to shell companies'. The advisory's footnote makes explicit that the mass-registration address flag captures a single address (often a TCSP) that 'manages a number of shell companies on behalf of its customers' -- i.e. multiple entities clustered at one address -- which is the shared-address network signature PAT005 names, distinct from the individual shell-company-trading indicator already claimed.
doctrine_summary: NI005 Common Address identifies entities connected through a shared address.

evidence.quote: A trade entity is registered at an address that is likely to be a mass registration address, e.g. high -density residential buildings, post -box addresses, commercial buildings or industrial complexes, especially when there is no reference to a specific unit.
This may also include the address of a trust and company service provider that manages a number of shell companies on behalf of its customers.

question: Should the ADV-2026-0002 label carry PAT005 Common Address?
